segments.text: A student investigated osmosis in pieces of potato.
This is the method used.
1. Cut a piece of potato into a cube.
2. Record the mass of the cube.
3. Place the cube into a beaker containing 0.4 mol/dm3 salt solution.
4. After some time, remove the cube and record the mass.
5. Calculate the change in the mass of the cube.
6. Repeat steps 1 to 5 using two more different concentrations of salt solution.
Evaluate the student’s method.
You should include how the student could improve the validity of their results.
[6 marks]
Level 3: A judgement, strongly linked and logically supported by a sufficient range of correct reasons, is given. 5–6
Level 2: Some logically linked reasons are given. There may also be a simple judgement. 3–4
Level 1: Relevant points are made. They are not logically linked. 1–2
No relevant content. 0
Indicative content:
(strengths)
• same / a / one plant / potato used
• all potato pieces used were cubes
• mass was recorded before and after
• change in mass was calculated
• different concentrations of salt solution were used
(improvement and reason)
• use the same / a / one potato for all pieces
o (because the student) may have used different potatoes
• remove skin or peel the potato
o (because) skin (may still be) present
• blot / dry cube before measuring mass
o (because) cube will have excess water on surface
• use same / set size / surface area of potato piece each time

o (because) size / surface area of cubes not controlled /
specified
• repeat (whole investigation or at each concentration)
o (because there were) no repeats
o to spot anomalies
• calculate mean (from repeats)
o (because there was) no mean calculated
• same time for each piece to be in solution
o (because) length of time in solution not specified
• control temperature of solution using water bath

o (because) temperature (of solution) not controlled /
specified

• use same volume of solution for each piece of potato  
or ensure all pieces are completely submerged
o (because) volume of solution not specified / controlled
• calculate percentage change in mass

o (because) percentage change in mass not calculated
or 
(because) each potato piece had a different starting mass
• include control experiment with boiled cube
o (because) no control experiment included
• increase the number of concentrations (of salt solution) used

o (because) only 3 different concentrations (of salt solution) 
used

For Level 3, a strength and improvements / reasons must be 
included.
This is an Extended Response question.

Please read the information in the introduction to this 
commentary document regarding how to annotate student’s responses.

You may find it helpful to download the infographic (star-chart) from the additional supporting 
information in OLS.

This shows what details are required to gain access (i.e. achieve the lower 
mark) for each Level in a visual format.

In the mark scheme, there are 5 strengths shown by a black dot and 12 improvements shown 
by a black dot and their corresponding reason(s) shown by a white dot(s).

Examiners are 
advised to number the ‘strengths’ bullet points in the mark scheme from 1-5 and the 
improvements and reasons from 1-12.

When using the star annotation for strengths, place the 
star on the left-hand side of the student’s response and the improvements and reasons on the 
right-hand side.

If the improvement and reason are linked, place the star icons next to each 
other.

To achieve entry to Level 3, the student must identify at least one strength from the method 
given at the start of the question.

There must also be a linked improvement and corresponding 
reason, along with additional improvements / reasons as indicated in the infographic.

For entry 
into Level 2, students must identify some improvements or reasons.

To achieve entry into Level 
1, a student can give a strength or an improvement or a reason.

If the student mentions ‘the potato’ this is not sufficient for credit in relation to using the same 
potato (as a strength BP or as an improvement BP).

However, if the student states ‘a potato’ or 
‘one potato’ credit should be awarded.

Take care not to award credit twice for the same potato 
being used as a strength, and as an improvement.
For BP5, the idea of ‘repeat’ without qualification is sufficient to gain credit.
